title: CHAPTER 13: ANDHRA PRADESH'S CONTRIBUTION TO INDIA

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Andhra Pradesh produced prominent national leaders who contributed significantly to India's governance and political landscape.
Sriharikota plays a paramount role in India's space and scientific advancement as the primary satellite launch center.
The state had a pivotal presence and active participation in various phases of the Indian Freedom Struggle.
Andhra Pradesh's contribution to the formation and evolution of the Indian Constitution remains a major milestone.

blocks.content: Sriharikota, located in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh, is home to the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), India's primary launch facility operated by ISRO. The island/peninsula is strategically located on the Bay of Bengal coast, facilitating rocket launches into geostationary and polar orbits. All major Indian rockets including PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) are launched from here. The center was renamed after Dr. Satish Dhawan, a distinguished aerospace scientist and former ISRO Chairman, in 2002.

Key milestones at SHAR include: India's first satellite Aryabhata (1975, though launched from a Soviet site), Chandrayan-1 (2008), Mangalyaan/Mars Orbiter Mission (2013), Chandrayaan-2 (2019), and Chandrayaan-3 (2023) – India's historic lunar soft landing.

blocks.content: 13.4 Andhra Pradesh in the Indian Constitution
Andhra Pradesh played a key role in shaping constitutional history:
(1) The demand for linguistic states was first successfully met in AP (Andhra State, 1953), leading to the States Reorganisation Act 1956 which reorganized all Indian states on linguistic lines.

items: Role of Sriharikota in ISRO's space missions and satellite launches is a recurring topic in Science & Tech.
Key political leaders and freedom fighters from Andhra Pradesh are frequently tested in Modern Indian History.
Constitutional provisions and reorganisation history of Andhra Pradesh are essential for Indian Polity questions.

blocks.content: (2) Potti Sriramulu's sacrifice highlighted that the constitution would need to accommodate linguistic identities of the Indian people, leading to a fundamental change in India's federal structure.
(3) The creation of Andhra Pradesh through merger of Andhra State and Hyderabad State's Telugu areas demonstrated the constitutional provisions for reorganization of states under Article 3.

(4) The bifurcation of 2014 (creation of Telangana) under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014 was the most recent major state reorganization in India, showing the continuing constitutional mechanism for state formation.
